questions.stem: What are the four traits of ACID?
options: Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation and Durability
Availability, Consistency, Integrity and Durability
Atomicity, Concurrency, Isolation and Distribution
Accuracy, Completeness, Integrity and Durability
Atomicity, Consistency, Indexing and Durability
questions.explanation: ACID stands for atomicity, consistency, isolation and durability.

options: That every query sees the latest committed value
That two users cannot update the same row at once
That data is completely written to the destination with no partial data left behind
That data survives a machine failure
That every table has a primary key
questions.explanation: Atomicity makes sure data is completely written in a destination with no partial data left behind.

options: That writes are never lost after a crash
That partial writes are rolled back
That each user has a private copy of the data
That all data is stored in the same file format
That once an operation is performed, its results are visible to every subsequent query
questions.explanation: Consistency ensures that after an application performs an operation, the results are visible to every next query, even if data is being updated or deleted while a user reads it.

options: That data is encrypted between nodes
That an incomplete operation by one user does not cause unexpected side effects for other users
That every operation is written to a transaction log
That queries run on a dedicated node
That operations complete in the order submitted
questions.explanation: Isolation ensures an incomplete operation by one user has no unexpected side effects on other users.

options: That the database can scale to petabytes
That queries always return within a fixed time
That data is never duplicated
That once an operation is completed, it is preserved even if the machine or system fails
That data can be read by every user simultaneously
questions.explanation: Durability means a completed operation is preserved even in the event of a machine or system failure.

questions.stem: The database Transaction Log, which holds every query statement run so that lost data can be reproduced, is given as an example of which ACID trait?
options: Atomicity
Durability
Isolation
Consistency
Availability
questions.explanation: The transaction log illustrates durability: because every statement is recorded, data can be reproduced if it is lost.

questions.stem: What is the relationship between ACID and Insert, Update and Delete operations?
options: ACID replaces the need for Insert, Update and Delete
Insert, Update and Delete are the four traits of ACID
ACID applies only to Select queries
ACID slows down Insert, Update and Delete so they should be avoided
ACID makes sure that while Insert, Update and Delete queries are happening, nothing impacts operational behaviour
questions.explanation: They have different functions but work together: ACID guarantees that Insert, Update and Delete operations do not disturb operational behaviour, and without ACID those functions are not reliable.

questions.stem: How can ACID capability be achieved in Hadoop via Hive?
options: By using ORC or Parquet file formats
By using CSV or JSON file formats
By disabling the transaction log
By storing data on tape
By using only structured data
questions.explanation: One way to get ACID and Insert, Update and Delete in Hadoop is to use ORC or Parquet file formats via Hive.

questions.stem: How does Databricks provide ACID capability through Delta Lake?
options: Using HDFS with any file format
Using a relational database as a side store
Using its compute layer over Hadoop
Using only Object Storage and only the Parquet file format
Using in-memory tables
questions.explanation: Databricks' Delta Lake delivers ACID capabilities using only Object Storage and only the Parquet file format.

questions.stem: In a nutshell, what is said about Insert, Update and Delete functions without ACID?
options: They run faster
They are only available in NoSQL databases
They are not reliable
They require Object Storage
They cannot be logged
questions.explanation: The summary is that Insert, Update and Delete functions are not reliable without ACID capability.
